title: A machine branching on a computed Boolean value
statement: Let $F$ be a machine format, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $p$ map Boolean strings to Boolean values. Suppose $M$ computes the one-symbol output $p(x)$ on every input $x$ within $c(|x|+1)$ steps for some natural number $c$. Then there are a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine $C$, an entry state, an injective assignment of exit states to Boolean values, and a natural number $a$, with at least one work tape, such that for every input $x$ there is a time $t\le a(|x|+1)$ at which $C$, started in its entry state with all work tapes blank, is in the exit state assigned to $p(x)$ with all work tapes blank; before time $t$, it is never in either exit state.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Turing machine $M$ over Boolean symbols
A Boolean-valued function $p$ on Boolean strings
A natural number $c$ giving the time bound
For every input, $M$ computes the one-symbol output $p(x)$ within $c(|x|+1)$ steps
